references.text: Moses predicts that the Lord will kill all the firstborn in Egypt, from Pharaoh's firstborn to the firstborn of the slave woman, as well as all the firstborn of livestock.
The Lord announces that He will go through Egypt this night and strike down all the firstborn, both humans and animals, and execute judgment on all the gods of Egypt.
Moses explains that the Lord killed all the firstborn in Egypt, both humans and animals, and therefore all firstborn must be consecrated to the Lord.
The Lord declares that all firstborn belong to Him from the day He struck down all the firstborn in Egypt.
The Lord confirms that all firstborn in Israel, both humans and animals, belong to Him because He struck down all the firstborn in Egypt.
The Egyptians buried their firstborn whom the Lord had struck among them, and the Lord had executed judgment on their gods.
The psalm describes how God struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, the first offspring in the tents of Ham.
The psalm reminds us that God struck down all the firstborn in their land, the firstfruits of all their strength.
The psalm praises the Lord who struck down Egypt's firstborn, both humans and animals.
The psalm extols the Lord who struck Egypt through their firstborn, for His mercy endures forever.
Hebrews mentions that Moses by faith instituted the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch the Israelites.
Prophetic precursor and direct fulfillment: The warning in chapter 11 is confirmed word for word in the event of chapter 12.
Prophetic proclamation: God's own voice announces the exact action carried out in 12:29.
